subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable batching/aggregation of outbound Telegram notifications

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in outbound Telegram notification digest policy, and should it live in the Telegram plugin, shared outbound delivery, or an external plugin/hook surface?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the contract affects config shape, delivery timing, urgent error bypass, media/thread semantics, persistence, and the core-versus-plugin boundary.

options.title: Define opt-in durable digest policy
options.body: Choose the owner seam, config names, bypass rules, and SQLite-backed flush behavior before implementation.

options.title: Require external plugin or hook extension
options.body: Keep core lean and add or document a missing plugin hook only if delayed aggregation cannot be built safely today.

options.title: Keep immediate delivery
options.body: Treat current streaming coalescing, throttling, and error cooldowns as the supported anti-spam mechanisms and narrow or close this request later.

recommendation.title: Define opt-in durable digest policy
recommendation.body: Choose the owner seam, config names, bypass rules, and SQLite-backed flush behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history signal across shared channel delivery and Telegram outbound surfaces involved in the product boundary choice.
